scores.evidence: The decisive choice was made while the race was stopped... Nobody could see it yet, but that was the race.
'What the timing data cannot see' functions as a limitations coda — not a summary restatement, but it does wrap and close the argument rather than simply ending on the last entry's final fact.
No bridging sentences detected between sections; headings do all transitional work throughout.

'From lap 40 to lap 48 the gap fell from 7.1s to 0.264s, a closing rate of 0.85 seconds per lap' — multiple figures clustered in a single sentence; also '13.7s', '31 seconds', '18 seconds' appear in close succession.
'that figure is an estimate rather than a measured counterfactual' and 'the price of the alternative is an estimate, labelled as one' — hedges are explicit and owned, not neutralising.
Russell is the consistent benchmark throughout: gap to Russell, tyre age relative to Russell, what Russell did at the VSC.
'RED FLAG - RACE SUSPENDED' and the stewards' penalty text used as hard evidentiary stops confirming the analytical point just made.
No recap of running order; 'The headline number needs its caveat at once' interprets rather than narrates.
'Verstappen made the same call at the same moment, took a hard tyre, and paid the same discounted price' — dry, flat, no exclamation.
'I think this is the part the 19th-to-first line hides' and 'I wonder if' absent — first person appears exactly once to flag a judgment call.
Names introduced bare, VSC/tyre offsets unexplained, pace delta assumed understood.
Paragraphs consistently 2-4 sentences; 'Nobody could see it yet, but that was the race' is a one-sentence standalone that works as a unit.
'The medium car was quicker on equal-age rubber and still could not pass.' following a long analytical sentence; rhythm is consistently varied.
'The rest of the grid' compresses Gasly's pole and Pérez's penalty into one paragraph — correct instinct, but Tsunoda's loose end and the 66-point standings tacked on dilute the coda discipline.

top_fixes: E1: Disaggregate the number cluster in the VSC section — '13.7s', '31 seconds', '18 seconds' should each anchor a separate claim rather than stacking in consecutive sentences; the arithmetic argument is the mechanism, so it deserves room to breathe one figure at a time.

S2/P3: The final 'What the timing data cannot see' section slides into a limitations disclaimer that functions as a summary wrapper; cut it to two sentences or fold the data-gap caveats into the relevant analytical sections so the piece ends on the last substantive fact rather than on a procedural note about the warehouse.

P3: 'The rest of the grid' stitches Gasly's pace degradation, Verstappen's mechanism, Pérez's penalty, Tsunoda's unresolved infringement, and the championship standings into one paragraph — significance is not signalled by length here; Gasly's collapse from pole deserves its own short entry, and the standings line should either go there or be cut.
